document.title: Colorado Academic Standards: Reading, Writing and Communicating

04075F0C722146BE8DBA2E254DCB6170.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

11E2C650D41B4041995B732FE1CE36BA.description: Develop the topic with relevant, well-chosen facts, definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples.

13CDD3E843DC4E9F8113950755F47428.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (for example: precede, recede, secede).

13DF52C7CC3F40D38AD36104DD3F3C2B.description: Interpret figures of speech (for example: verbal irony, puns) in context.

1797C4E0432649EC8F4072C9E7483239.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.

18C3A7A8AC0844F180B2AC8AD2A94690.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic.

1AAC8ED7333B4910B7D4985440712B51.description: Write well-organized and cohesive arguments, distinguishing claim(s) from opposing claims and using language to clarify connections among claims, reasons, and evidence.

1DC938928E9A42F4A0E2C58940E4E7CF.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and present the relationships between information and ideas efficiently as well as to interact and collaborate with others.

27462C1F972B44E889562C8DF7793C0A.description: Determine a central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including its relationship to supporting ideas; provide an objective summary of the text.

287148372429490FA75CE4D692149DAA.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including analogies or allusions to other texts.

2B90DEC09FCA4CF7B97B4400508A3C8D.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

2C6C97D1568B4A2DBD9FA7886901B846.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at the high end of the grades 6–8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

2C9881F8DBBF4EB9B39723BE5A23BA34.description: Analyze how a modern work of fiction draws on themes, patterns of events, or character types from myths, traditional stories, or religious works such as the Bible, including describing how the material is rendered new.

2D6B3FAE01B64C028F82FA91FB8D80A4.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

2E7E60E57CF148D8A853330FBA46533A.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (for example: by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

31335A8C5D9F4DE1968A14A3BC596852.description: Use precise words and phrases, relevant descriptive details, and sensory language to capture the action and convey experiences and events.

34D7856183C948DFBF8E0FB92D94EC20.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

356A39E3C50E4E0DAF6C418E26772FB2.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, using search terms effectively; assess the credibility and accuracy of each source; and quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

368659A0EACA430EAE1D3344A5B80BC5.description: Use verbs in the active and passive voice and in the conditional and subjunctive mood to achieve particular effects (for example: emphasizing the actor or the action; expressing uncertainty or describing a state contrary to fact).

37BA0215B93D4B3E97FC3A23B791BA68.description: Use the relationship between particular words to better understand each of the words.

38DF0DB4F4634050A0804D7A8B8524EC.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

390DA8224875419C81B49F99CA4E5649.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on the narrated experiences or events.

3A7AA6D673B849CC8E434C83948A094E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style.

3AB00E19CBF0428FAF5CDF602FA4F6E3.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings; analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone, including analogies or allusions to other texts.

3E945C48DA3542439014D6A82DABF32B.description: Use Range of Reading and Complexity of Text to:

43CD131FFDFF4116ADBA5B5A1A065C94.description: Cite the textual evidence that most strongly supports an analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

44888E17AF9E4611854ECA0C9F344B85.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

47FFF008F49B4D5FB1BCA9EF657FFED4.description: Introduce claim(s), acknowledge and distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and organize the reasons and evidence logically.

488773424AD245488ED89C25D1BA234A.description: Engage and orient the reader by establishing a context and point of view and introducing a narrator and/or characters; organize an event sequence that unfolds naturally and logically.

4ECF60955F4D4C3F83B8ACA5ADA563B8.description: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence.

4FC7A440755E47238CD909358DBA4DF7.description: Use Key Ideas and Details to:

5034C21F00D54538B528D7322A1B36F6.description: Compare and contrast the structure of two or more texts and analyze how the differing structure of each text contributes to its meaning and style.

5504B176B23D49428F10A73D67B04D71.description: Evaluate the advantages and disadvantages of using different mediums (for example: print or digital text, video, multimedia) to present a particular topic or idea.

5627F8051E214916BF6A1D27C4145DF6.description: Follow rules for collegial discussions and decision-making, track progress toward specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.

58F21C88F7CC4715962D5D41223B9742.description: Use punctuation (comma, ellipsis, dash) to indicate a pause or break.

5E51D275FB95498F8A078FACED44252C.description: Acknowledge new information expressed by others, and, when warranted, qualify or justify their own views in light of the evidence presented.

61C937EFC17747E4BAA1B89570717482.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; recognize when irrelevant evidence is introduced.

662BC20F6BC1444993DAD62E4A60A029.description: Apply grade 8 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (for example: "Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is sound and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; recognize when irrelevant evidence is introduced").

673E5D6C04984AFBB37B5B98C6309669.description: Integrate multimedia and visual displays into presentations to clarify information, strengthen claims and evidence, and add interest.

6C9A5774F0054D88A5A5AB583A6FF064.description: Pose important questions; identify, locate, and evaluate sources; extract and synthesize relevant information, and communicate findings appropriately.

6D926F37C9CD4D40B62F0BAA37C30914.description: Design organized presentations incorporating key details and claims while tailored for purpose and audience.

6E92ECDD960F4164AE6DBEB725256A01.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

6EEB838425D848CEA1E936C1486F9549.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

73EA525821284D61B512D14AA1B8F3B2.description: Analyze how a text makes connections among and distinctions between individuals, ideas, or events (for example: through comparisons, analogies, or categories).

742ECCAB13D6448D8AD4B35662AE5F70.description: Write engaging real or imagined narratives effectively using techniques such as relevant and sufficient descriptive details, sensory language, logical pacing and dialogue to detail actions and to develop and reflect on experiences and events.

76EE9A0F6C044F07A823CEA9B88D7ADB.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question), drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions that allow for multiple avenues of exploration.

7B296D1F986E4158A8E66B49C75A82C3.description: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, evaluating the soundness of the reasoning and relevance and sufficiency of the evidence and identifying when irrelevant evidence is introduced.

7CF867CD4A024E8E94CB7917B0915131.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, and reflection, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

7ECC2647EFF74485AED828666DD5D731.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including its relationship to the characters, setting, and plot; provide an objective summary of the text.

82375ACB6A1747859A112E8FB703D2B2.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

84EE89D654674B35AD5201D31C3864A1.description: Analyze in detail the structure of a specific paragraph in a text, including the role of particular sentences in developing and refining a key concept.

8511573DBE9B430883035938D4DC6D83.description: Analyze a case in which two or more texts provide conflicting information on the same topic and identify where the texts disagree on matters of fact or interpretation.

85A3CD4B085744D18BFFF3ED756391D3.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 8 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

8648E85E0D7C408C9A03A84312C07E35.description: Analyze the purpose of information presented in diverse media and formats (for example: visually, quantitatively, orally) and evaluate the motives (for example: social, commercial, political) behind its presentation.

89753B4B35C24EB8822DDB5A8D304C70.description: Apply knowledge of word structure, grammar, and context to determine the meaning of new words and phrases in increasingly complex texts.

8E9A106CBB144FA491C9C9F1D5C3B4E2.description: Use a variety of transition words, phrases, and clauses to convey sequence, signal shifts from one time frame or setting to another, and show the relationships among experiences and events.

91A04C6A01F14E8B900075C161498C39.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (for example: dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

91C30982556D46D3ACD13944ACCADC6A.description: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:

9342ADF7B6074BEA84BEFFDAA39E267F.description: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:

9A2F9BBB5DB54694BB8D8D44A14F9E27.description: Explain the function of verbals (gerunds, participles, infinitives) in general and their function in particular sentences.

9C7C9F205DD6415EB5ED93A09CF472E9.description: Engage in effective collaborative discussions and analyze information presented.

A00D8D2C6FBF4126AD2B1EF86223483F.description: Analyze the extent to which a filmed or live production of a story or drama stays faithful to or departs from the text or script, evaluating the choices made by the director or actors.

A02C6AA128A24DCAA6B70D8C343206FF.description: Analyze how differences in the points of view of the characters and the audience or reader (for example: created through the use of dramatic irony) create such effects as suspense or humor.

A44F30EE5E814504A2C13AFE2ADB2D89.description: Form and use verbs in the active and passive voice.

A667A4B54EC648C4AB670ECB89F05924.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

A7F216519EC64A408D957213788E403C.description: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (for example: bullheaded, willful, firm, persistent, resolute).

AA78E309FD854381AF86CB76FC795A45.description: Correctly spell frequently used words and consult reference materials (for example: dictionaries, both print and digital, spell check, and/or trusted peers and/or adults) to determine the spelling of less frequent vocabulary.

AA993A9FB22249318DD749EF6F1B6491.description: Write well-developed and logically organized informative/explanatory texts, conveying relevant content through precise language, domain-specific vocabulary, and formal style.

AAC836DD94694615AF26F7CCCC610C25.description: Analyze and evaluate an author's choices to understand informational text.

ABC9853177114470B282F7409DF9BBE5.description: Pose questions that connect the ideas of several speakers and respond to others' questions and comments with relevant evidence, observations, and ideas.

ADE4D5B7495A46A79D9EAD1B682F4EBE.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, relevant descriptive details, and well-structured event sequences.

AEE5497BD54E406E83AF20A2DAE180AF.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented.

AF64B2EDA9F849DBA42B398903DC12CF.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content.

B084174C08634FA7801E02D1E85BDC75.description: Support claim(s) with logical reasoning and relevant evidence, using accurate, credible sources and demonstrating an understanding of the topic or text.

BDD4BF272C4542D6ABB08D7815693CAD.description: Use context (for example: the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

C19019C1AD6444D89D7D4A7015F90B45.description: Use an ellipsis to indicate an omission.

C301591BB5B746FCA29FCEFC3EF7ECA8.description: Use Key Ideas and Details to:

CBE38CC223CB4002AC9455FE8BF9CB81.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

CEA4CB888D364F32AB4322D1B7F95045.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, at the high end of grades 6–8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

D461AE9D27694951B74EE784BC999619.description: Analyze and evaluate literary elements and an author's choices to understand literary text.

D50C6D43F1CD47BCA08B570AB65D19D2.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words or phrases based on grade 8 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

D51271EA57664C1E9AE48D7B387EB69B.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information into broader categories; include formatting (for example: headings), graphics (for example: charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

D72E87374C8548E0B0432CB2837EDB51.description: Apply grade 8 Reading standards to literature (for example: "Analyze how a modern work of fiction draws on themes, patterns of events, or character types from myths, traditional stories, or religious works such as the Bible, including describing how the material is rendered new").

DA94660FCF7A401480C06DF5E835D7AD.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

E3E190DFCDE4436288808BF36138608A.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on ideas under discussion.

E4A7AE0048204F558ED25A1EA8633A19.description: Present claims and findings, emphasizing salient points in a focused, coherent manner with relevant evidence, sound valid reasoning, and well-chosen details; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation.

EA12B0D607A6469887D4E19710D66607.description: Produce clear and coherent final drafts that demonstrate a command of the conventions for grammar, usage, and mechanics as well as a style appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

EE616E85F00C459CAB61A9CA6D435B88.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how the author acknowledges and responds to conflicting evidence or viewpoints.

F5F616A90FD945D9B6CC9FA93B2D5F1A.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in verb voice and mood.

F7489B354A2D4705BFA790F751B5A8B8.description: Cite the textual evidence that most strongly supports an analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

F7F7EF8B6C0B461F9D9FD9CF6D52BD30.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

F9A34AE23F2D4D7C977DC4963069850C.description: Form and use verbs in the indicative, imperative, interrogative, conditional, and subjunctive mood.

FAB380A9350D408D91B681494339823A.description: Use stylistic techniques (for example: alliteration, onomatopoeia); figurative language (for example: simile, metaphor, personification, hyperbole); and graphic elements (for example: capital letters, line length, word position) to express personal or narrative voice.

FCF19C5EF7654C2892687049D6C3CE3D.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to create cohesion and clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.

FEB72D34399740DC93A49F1FF079265E.description: Analyze how particular lines of dialogue or incidents in a story or drama propel the action, reveal aspects of a character, or provoke a decision.
